title: Parametric eval harness for detecting config-change blindspots
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Recent incidents surfaced quality regressions after config and model variant rollouts where existing smoke evals missed narrow but severe quality cliffs. Postmortems call out two recurring gaps: (1) our eval suites validate a single nominal config per route, and (2) we lack a lightweight, parameter-sweep runner that can probe low-probability config combinations (e.g., long-prefix KV + aggressive batching + q4f quantization).

Goal: Build a parametric evaluation harness and assertion library that can run fast, targeted sweeps across a configurable matrix of runtime/model parameters (kv_ttl, batch_size, qconfig, kernel_variant, max_seq, temperature) and surface regression deltas with artifactized repro cases and minimal-resource execution. This harness should be usable by postmortem owners, CI gates for config rollouts, and scheduled scavenger jobs that look for quality cliffs in production-like slices.

Scope (MVP):
- Parametric runner service that accepts a small YAML matrix and executes a suite of evals in parallel with early-fail signal aggregation.
- An assertion DSL (JSON/YAML) with common metrics (exact match, logprob delta, canonicalized BLEU/F1, hallucination flags) and a way to declare per-route tolerances.
- Auto-capture of minimal repro (input + model/config snapshot + seed) and upload to the eval artifacts bucket with a short permalink.
- Dashboardable output: per-cell metric diffs, heatmap export, and suggested triage label.
- Lightweight CI integration: a pre-deploy job that runs a small sweep (3x3 matrix) for config changes and fails the rollout when assertions trip with high confidence.

Out of scope (for this ticket): full integration with the canonical eval oracle library, long-running golden-corpus backfills, and UI polish in Console. Those will be follow-ups.

Acceptance criteria:
- Harness can run a 12-cell matrix (3 params x 4 values) on staging within 45 minutes using burst pool.
- For a seeded synthetic regression (created as part of this ticket) the harness surfaces a metric regression >= 5% on the targeted slice and produces a reproducible artifact link.
- CI job template exists and is documented; at least one config PR uses the template and demonstrates a blocked rollout when assertions fail.
- Library of 6 assertion templates checked into repo (exact-match, top-k token shift, mean logprob delta, response-length-regression, hallucination-count, structured-field-mismatch).

Approach / Implementation plan:
1) Design: (Samir + Aisha) finalize the param space schema and assertion DSL. Draft in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/EVAL/Parametric+Eval+DSL (link is working draft).
2) Prototype runner: lightweight Python service that schedules eval jobs to the existing eval-worker pool, supports concurrency limits, and uploads artifacts to gs://redwood-eval-artifacts/parametric/ENG-49127.
3) Assertion library: implement metric hooks using existing eval metrics code but with wrapper that tolerates numeric jitter and reports CI-friendly pass/fail.
4) Minimal repro capture: enforce deterministic seeding, collect model config + runtime flags, store a 1-2MB JSON repro artifact with link in the harness results.
5) CI integration: add GitHub Action workflow template .github/workflows/parametric-sanity.yml that invokes a 3x3 sweep against a staging model.
6) Dashboard: emit a compact JSON summary that Console’s infra can ingest; provide temporary Kibana dashboard link for triage.

Tradeoffs / discussion points:
- Running larger matrices increases coverage but also cost; default will favor targeted slices defined by incident owners.
- We will intentionally keep the assertion DSL small to start (no programmatic transforms) to encourage FRs instead of complexity.
- For deterministic repro we may need temporary snapshotting of model weights or model hash; for now we'll capture model artifact id and runtime flags.

Risks and mitigations:
- False positives from noisy metrics: mitigate with confidence intervals and repeated sampling.
- CI latency: default CI template uses small sample sizes; full sweeps reserved for scheduled runs.
- Access control for artifact links: store artifacts in private bucket with short-lived signed URLs for triage links.

Deliverables:
- repo: infra/evals/parametric-harness (prototype + CI template)
- Confluence design doc + examples: link above
- Demo PR that blocks a sample config rollout in staging and attaches a repro artifact
- One-pager for on-call/postmortem runbook on using the harness for incident follow-ups

Notes: This ticket aims to reduce the time-to-repro and increase coverage for edge config combos without turning on combinatorial sweeps in production by default. The harness should be easy to extend by PM/Eng incident owners to codify 'slices we care about'.
